builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Alania-2: Turkish text-to-speech with instant and fine-tuned voice cloning
summary: This approach replaces reliance on massive real-world audio corpora and foundation-scale models by training a compact 488M-parameter system on 18,195 hours of teacher-generated synthetic speech (90% of data) combined with deterministic text normalization rules. The costs involve implementing normalization logic, curating the teacher model, and engineering diffusion inference to achieve 32ms first-audio latency. Failures include inability to synthesize alphanumeric strings or loanwords without the normalizer, and instant voice cloning exhibiting 21.9% word omission unless conditioned to continue the reference audio rather than clone from it.
rationale: This demonstrates that domain-specific synthetic data and rule-based text normalization enable small teams with constrained infrastructure to deploy high-quality TTS without training foundation models or requiring massive compute clusters.
technique: Synthetic data distillation and text normalization for TTS

claims.statement: This approach replaces reliance on massive real-world audio corpora and foundation-scale models by training a compact 488M-parameter system on 18,195 hours of teacher-generated synthetic speech (90% of data) combined with deterministic text normalization rules. The costs involve implementing normalization logic, curating the teacher model, and engineering diffusion inference to achieve 32ms first-audio latency. Failures include inability to synthesize alphanumeric strings or loanwords without the normalizer, and instant voice cloning exhibiting 21.9% word omission unless conditioned to continue the reference audio rather than clone from it.

Text normalization reduced word error rate from complete failure (0/96 sentences critical parts correct) to 86/96 correct; voice cloning conditioning on reference audio alone cut skipped words from 21.9% to 1.7%.
